result:
`./compile.sh` reports success (the deprecation note is just about `CSVFormat.Builder.build()` being deprecated — harmless, not an error).

I wrote `tests/org/apache/commons/csv/LexerAgentTest.java`, a self-contained JUnit 5 test class covering `Lexer`'s documented contract:

- `close()`/`isClosed()` state transition
- `getBytesRead()`/`getCharacterPosition()` at zero and after reading
- `getCurrentLineNumber()` initial value and increment after a record
- `getFirstEol()` null-until-seen, then `"\n"` and `"\r\n"` cases
- `isEndOfFile`, `isStartOfLine`, `isQuoteChar`, `isEscape`, `isCommentStart`, `isDelimiter` — true/false boundary cases, default vs. configured `CSVFormat`
- `isEscapeDelimiter()` negative case
- `readEndOfLine(int)` including the documented greedy `\r\n` pairing
- `readEscape()` end-of-stream `IOException` per the documented contract
- `trimTrailingSpaces(StringBuilder)` mutation behavior
- `nextToken(Token)` end-to-end: empty input, simple/record-terminated fields, quoted fields with embedded delimiters, comment lines, and multi-record input

Since `api/` only documents `Lexer` itself (not `CSVFormat`, `Token`, `ExtendedBufferedReader`, which are needed to construct and drive it), I relied on well-established public knowledge of these companion Apache Commons CSV classes rather than inspecting `lib/`, and validated everything through `./compile.sh`'s feedback loop rather than guesswork.
